messages:
sam (support): FYI new SEV from Straylight — they hit sustained 429s during today's morning batch. Customers say 'burst credits depleted' and requests were queued for ~30s. Attaching customer logs excerpt.

emma (oncall-sre): looking now. I can already see admission_controller.rejected spiking at 2025-11-03T09:12:04Z -> many requests hit admission fallback. Client error 429 correlated with burst_credit_remaining = 0.

javier (infra): pulling the dedicated pool metrics for pool id dp-17. GPU utilization climbed but not full saturation. However we have a single tenant (straylight) + a noisy tenant on same pool that had a short intense fanout. Possible headroom mis-config.

claire (cs): Straylight reports intermittent 401s around the same time. They had multiple concurrent token refresh attempts; some downstream auth requests returned 502 which cascaded.

sam (support): pasted logs from customer:
```
2025-11-03T09:12:02Z request_id=abc123 status=429 reason="burst credits exhausted"
2025-11-03T09:12:04Z request_id=abc124 status=401 auth_error="token refresh failed"
```

emma (oncall-sre): admission controller thresholds show capacity = 25k tps, admission_threshold = 22k (0.88). We saw a sudden delta where effective offered load briefly spiked to 27k — that pushed admission to reject until credits were replenished.

javier (infra): quick repro steps if you need to run locally (use dedicated staging pool):
1) warm KV cache: send a long prefix stream of 2k short requests
2) burst generator: for i in {1..5000}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <tok>" -d '{"prompt":"x"}' https://staging-infer:443/generate &
This reproduces admission.rejected within ~20s on a 10k cap pool.

emma (oncall-sre): immediate mitigations we applied:
- bumped admission_headroom to 0.15 (was 0.08) for the affected pool
- enabled temporary route-level reserve for Straylight's critical route (reserve_tokens=2000)
- fallback policy enabled to route critical requests to a compatible lower-cost model variant (4-bit quantized) to keep latency SLOs

sam (support): Straylight accepted fallback for ~10m and errors dropped to normal. They still want root cause and a plan to avoid this.

javier (infra): long-term recommendations:
- plan headroom: set headroom to max(15%, traffic_variance_pct) per pool, and run 72h traffic variance job to size
- add per-tenant soft reservations for high-criticality customers so noisy neighbors can't sweep credits
- tweak autoscaler to react on queue length + admission_reject_rate rather than util alone (reduces 20–30s cold gap)
- increase burst_credit_replenish_rate for dedicated pools with bursty OLTP workloads

claire (cs): I'll offer Straylight a short-term credit buffer and collect their peak cadence so infra can size a Dedicated scaled artifact.

billing-bot: alert: account=straylight burst_credits_used=100% period=60m action="noted"

deploy-bot: canary notice: changed admission_headroom for pool dp-17 by +0.07 (automated rollback window 15m)

emma (oncall-sre): follow ups: 1) infra to run headroom sizing job and share numbers by EOD; 2) infra/sre to draft a playbook for noisy-neighbor detection and per-tenant reserves; 3) support+cs to coordinate customer comms + temporary credit; 4) a post-incident doc and calendar PM for capacity tuning next week.

sam (support): noted. tagging @javier @emma for action items. I'll keep thread updated with customer replies.

claire (cs): Straylight said they can provide a 48h trace of traffic if infra wants deeper analysis. Also asked whether we can schedule a short architecture review about isolation options.

javier (infra): please send the trace. I'll also add a short config checklist to the playbook: `admission.headroom`, `burst.credit_replenish`, `route.reserve_tokens`, `autoscale.scale_on_queue`.

emma (oncall-sre): adding to incident backlog: IR-2025-347 - dedicated-burst-headroom-misconfig. Assign to infra and oncall for remediation and postmortem.

sam (support): thanks — will update thread when we have the postmortem link and customer follow-up."
